newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 to $15 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 to $15 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 to $15 higher Tuesday as a weaker dollar against Sterling is expected to draw currency-linked buying in New York.
"It's all currency," one trader said. "The sterling's up."

Sterling initially rallied more than a cent against the dollar Tuesday after the U.K. raised its base rate 25 basis points, as expected, and announced new central bank freedom to set interest rate policy.

LIFFE cocoa futures were flat to firmer in rangebound trade early Tuesday, buoyed by industry-linked buying in the back months. At the midday break, July was unchanged at 995 stg a tonne, with September up four stg at 1,015 stg.

Monday, New York cocoa futures posted modest gains in thin trading. July ended up $6 at $1,385 a tonne after ranging from $1,401 to $1,374. Spot May ended up the same at $1,374, while the back months gained $2 to $4.

Technically, traders pegged July near-term resistance at Monday's high of $1,401. Major resistance awaited at $1,416-$1,418. Support was seen at $1,365-1,360, with a push through that level leading to a test of $1,330. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
